newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain says will not attend Gulf Arab summit.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain says will not attend Gulf Arab summit.

text.p: Bahrain said on Wednesday it would not attend a Gulf Arab summit next month in Qatar, which has taken a territorial dispute with Bahrain to the International Court of Justice.

"Bahrain will not take part in meetings being held in Qatar because of unfriendly attitudes Qatar is taking against Bahrain," Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa told the official Gulf News Agency.
The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- grouping Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates -- is to hold its annual summit in the Qatari capital Doha on December 7.
Qatar reacted by saying it hoped Bahrain would review its boycott decision.
"We are not surprised (by Bahrain's move) but we wish they would review their stand," a senior foreign ministry official told Reuters.

GCC leaders, including secretary-general Jameel Hujilan of Saudi Arabia, have been trying to persuade Bahrain to drop its threat to boycott the summit over its territorial dispute with neighbouring Qatar.
Qatar has gone to the International Court of Justice in The Hague over a small group of barren but potentially valuable islands, sandbanks and reefs controlled by Bahrain but claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has said it would only withdraw the court case if Saudi Arabia's mediation succeeded in resolving the dispute.
